added_lines: today - thirtieth sunday in ordinary time you shall not wrong a soujourner immigration has become a fraught political subject. the global wealth inequality, particularly between the northern hemisphere compared to the southern hemisphere, has led to mass migration of peoples seeking a better life for themselves and their children. the catechism of the catholic church does recognise the right of states to restrict their borders: “political authorities, for the sake of the common good for which they are responsible, may make the exercise of the right to immigrate subject to various juridical conditions, especially with regarc to the immigrants’ duties toward their country of adoption. immigrants are obliged to respect with gratitude the material and spiritual heritage of the country that receives them, to obey its laws, and to assist in carrying civic burdens.” (catechism of the catholic church §2241). those who migrate into another country must be treated with dignity and respect. pope leo xvi, in his homily at the mass 4th july 2026 on the italian island of lampedusa said of the challenges of migration: "europe is capable of addressing the crisis in this region in a comprehensive manner, integrating immediate relief efforts into a long-term strategic plan capable of receiving, protecting, supporting and integrating migrants" while "assisting developing countries so that no one is forced to emigrate." we live in a country with a history where millions were forced to immigrate to other lands due to economic deprivation at home. pope john xxiii wrote in pacem in terris (§25, 1963): “every human being has the right to the freedom of movement and of residence within the confines of their country; and, when there are just reasons for it, the right to emigrate and take up residence elsewhere.” pope leo xvi reminds us that human dignity does not have a passport and does not lose value when a border is crossed. on world refugee day 11" june 2026 on the island of gran canaria he said: “human dignity demands legal and safe pathways, rescue and assistance, real cooperation against traffickers, effective protection for victims, serious processes of reception and integration, and policies that allow every person to live with dignity in their own land.” catholic communities must play their part in assisting and helping to integrate those who immigrate into our country. 30'" week in ordinary time, monday 26th october 8am mass: special intention 10.30am mass: mary conway (anniversary) 30'" week in ordinary time, tuesday 27th october t. otteran, mo optional memoria 8am mass: special intention 10.30am mass: ruenda liaban & pat keane (anniversary) 30'" week in ordinary time, wednesday 28th october ss. simon & jude, apostles (feast) 8am mass: special intention 10.30am mass
